idea: Watch one property move through one connected system. 14 Wattle Grove arrives as a single enquiry, waits while today's scattered tools fail to answer it, and then travels through Aurixa Systems: research, financial analysis, the client's report, the professional team's portals, the agent's draft and the professional's own judgement, to a recorded decision and a 14-day trial. Every frame is the product working, readable, or a graphic drawn in the product's own design system.

voiceover.timed_from: audio_preparations c47a30e0-edcd-4389-b98f-6c3fa11887d7 (265 measured words and speech segments)

keeps: The master voiceover, verbatim and never stretched: 106.031 s, speech ending at 105.88 s. Since the third cut it is held open in its own silences (pacing.py: 51 pauses between its measured speech segments, each a whole number of frames), so the film runs to the music's last downbeat and its ring.
Its cut points. Each block starts where the working master's block starts, and every new cut uses the spec's timing rule (in the pause before a word, else 0.1 s ahead, on the 30 fps grid).

The 45 captions, verbatim, at most two lines; none over the Block 14 phrases or the closing card. Since 22 October 2026, at the client's direction, set in the brand's own type and moving (scripts/aurixa-reel-1/captions.cjs): Playfair Display Medium, the site's headline face, in its silver headline gradient, one phrase a line in its italic (silver before the brand arrives, gold after, where a gold hairline draws under it and the light crosses it once), each word rising into focus on its spoken time (the voiceover's measured words), on a panel that reshapes from line to line: a white card of today's tools before the brand, the site's glass after.
The Block 14 phrases (PL-14A-1 to PL-14A-4) at the edit's own times.
The closing card (PL-15A), complete from the first frame of Block 15 through the audio tail.

The record, since the third cut a mock address at the client's direction: 14 Wattle Grove, Banksia Rise NSW 2155 (Banksia Rise is not a real suburb), stock reference WG-14, the property image P and a floor plan drawn new for this cut, still at the evaluation stage, graded A+ on a composite of 84 across all five dimensions in the product's own words (STRONG BUY - Excellent investment opportunity with strong fundamentals across all metrics).
The names, now only as accounts and records on screen: Jordan Ellis (client), Alex Morgan, Jamie Chen, Priya Shah, Mia Patel, Daniel Reed.
A Demo workspace label on every Aurixa screen, and fictional demonstration data only.

Every don't in the pack's brand guidelines, and the twelve guardrails of the studio's Aurixa Systems kit (docs/brands/aurixa-systems.md): no fabricated returns, approvals, valuations or results; no automatic financial, legal or accounting decision; no NPC wording; Aurixa Systems, AURIXA SYSTEMS and Aurixa Agent spelled exactly.

replaces.pack: People, hands, faces, rooms and sets, and the cast's sheets and Soul IDs
replaces.now: None appear. The product is the cast. (The six characters and their approved Soul IDs stay in the studio, unused here.)

None, but for the logo's moments, which the client asked to be made with a video model (22 October 2026): 04.1's reveal and the logo alive on the trial and closing cards are footage of the logo's clean plate (the supplied art with its lettering taken out), and the supplied lettering and emblem are laid over it, so no letter is ever drawn by a model. Every other frame is rendered from code: the products' pages as the reel's plates already rebuild them, and graphics written in the brand's CSS. Text is exact and sharp by construction.

replaces.pack: "Each portal demonstration must show a real hand using a mouse, keyboard or touchpad"
replaces.now: Each portal demonstration shows the product's own pointer, the control under it, the press, and the product's own response, in that order.

replaces.pack: "60 percent people and property, 25 percent platform, 15 percent architecture"
replaces.now: About 70 percent screen actions and workflows, 20 percent deliverables, 10 percent brand graphics (an editorial intention, as before).
A colour progression instead: the unbranded tools of today in plain light greys (Blocks 01 to 03, and 09.1), then the brand's deep navy and gold from Block 04 on.

replaces.pack: "Do not insert raw source screenshots into the film"
replaces.now: Kept, and it matters more now: the supplied screenshots carry real client names, addresses and personal bookmarks. They remain the structural reference; every screen in the film is the code-built page with the demo record.

screen_rules: One action per shot beat, and a result held at least 0.8 s before anything else moves (the montage 12.1 is the one exception).

The pointer is the product's: a standard arrow at 1.6 times its size so it reads on a phone, white with a dark edge. It travels on a gentle curve (the products' emphasized ease) and never jumps. A press is the control's own pressed state plus a fine ring in the focus cyan that grows and fades over the products' slow step, 320 ms.
Typing appears at a reading pace (about 16 characters a second) with the product's own caret.
Toasts, progress and page changes are the product's own components with their own timing.
A screen only changes because of an action the viewer sees, and only to the page that action really opens.
Anything the voiceover names is at least 22 px tall on the final 1080 x 1920 frame; smaller text is context, never the point.

Desktop pages keep their desktop layout, at the zoom their plates were drawn at, inside a window: the frame opens on the whole window for orientation, then a virtual camera moves in on the part that acts.

design.intro: The brand is written down four times, in four repositories, and they do not agree. This edition takes its graphics from the one the others name as their source: the public site's `@theme` (aurixa-systems, `src/index.css`). The Builders Network's `tokens.css` is that palette converted to HSL, and Mission Control's `aurixa-brand.ts` says its values are lifted verbatim from it. The scales the site never declares (radius, depth, glass and motion) come from the products' own `tokens.css`, where npc-client-dashboard and aurixa-builders declare the same values. The products' pages keep their own look, as the live product shows it. Every value below was read from the code on 21 October 2026 and names the file it is declared in.

sections.title: Shape, depth, glass and motion
sections.text: The site declares none of these (its panels are square, 2 px), so they come from the products' `tokens.css`, where npc-client-dashboard and aurixa-builders declare the same values. One rule decides between the two shapes: anything that holds the product (a window, a card) is the product's, rounded and glass; anything that is only the brand (an eyebrow, a corner, a rule) is the site's, square and 1 px. The durations are a control's; a camera move or a window's arrival takes its beat's own length, on the same curves.

sections.title: The stylesheet the renders read
sections.text: The graphics kit reads one stylesheet, `aurixa-reel.css` (beside this brief): a custom property for every role below, each with a comment naming the repository, file and line it is declared on. Xeno Studio's code scanner writes it from the four repositories (`scripts/aurixa-reel-1/reel_css.ts`), so a change to the brand's code reaches the reel by scanning again, never by retyping a value. Each role is read from the code and checked against this table: the 35 that name code all hold the value below, and the other 2 (plain white and the system face) name none. `aurixa-reel-tokens.png` draws every token as the code declares it.

G-WINDOW.name: The glass window
G-WINDOW.what: The Aurixa pages' holder: the page at its drawn zoom inside a rounded window of the products' own glass (fill, sheen and hairline stroke), lifted by their largest glass shadow, floating on the site's ground in the frame's action zone.

G-WINDOW-PLAIN.name: The plain window
G-WINDOW-PLAIN.what: The same window for today's tools: white, a grey system title bar, the system's own type, no brand colour and no glass.

G-POINTER.name: The pointer and its press
G-POINTER.what: A standard arrow at 1.6x, white with a dark edge, moving on the products' emphasized ease; a press draws a 1 px ring in the focus cyan that grows from 0 to 24 px and fades over 320 ms.

G-FOCUS.name: Focus corners
G-FOCUS.what: The site's own corner marks (.compliance-corners): a 1 px cyan corner top left and a gold one bottom right, 1rem long, closing in on the part of a page that acts.

G-RAIL.name: The journey rail
G-RAIL.what: Research · Financial · Report · Team · Decision, set in the site's eyebrow (mono, .28em, uppercase) on a panel strip above the window; the current stage in gold ink with the eyebrow's gold rule, the ones passed ticked, the rest muted. The film's one recurring chapter device.

G-SYSTEM-MAP.name: The system map
G-SYSTEM-MAP.what: The Command Centre as the hub, five portal windows around it (Client, Finance, Accountant, Solicitor, Builders Network), each on its own dashboard, on the site's cyan dot field. Each is joined to the hub by the site's rail line (cyan to gold), which draws in; a traveller dot runs along a line when something passes along it. Labels in the eyebrow mono on panel chips; the Builders Network window carries its own teal. Never rotates.

G-RECORD-CARD.name: The record card
G-RECORD-CARD.what: 14 Wattle Grove · WG-14 with the image P: the object the film follows. The same card in every scene it appears in, its title in the display serif, settling on the products' ease-out.

G-LINKS.name: Links
G-LINKS.what: The site's rail line (1 px, cyan to gold) drawn from one card to another, with a traveller dot that runs it once and settles; used for the team ringing the record.

G-DOCUMENT.name: The document
G-DOCUMENT.what: A PDF that lifts off a page as an object: its cover in front, its pages fanned behind, each the report's own page as the product prints it, with the products' deepest elevation beneath. The floor plan travels between portals as the same object.

G-HIGHLIGHT.name: The marker
G-HIGHLIGHT.what: The eyebrow's 1 px gold rule, drawn under the passage the voiceover points to and under the words the professional types.

G-HAIRLINE.name: The hairline
G-HAIRLINE.what: One gold line drawn across the frame on the site's ground, with the traveller's gold glow at its leading end: the turn from today's tools to Aurixa.

G-EMBLEM.name: The emblem build
G-EMBLEM.what: The supplied logo, at half the frame's width, revealed out of the night by a video model's take of its clean plate that ends exactly on the supplied art; then its own lettering, the art's pixels and the shadow they stand in, rising letter by letter and the light crossing it once; then the emblem, the supplied file, lifts into the Command Centre. The logo is the supplied file, never redrawn or retyped.

G-WALL.name: The wall of screens
G-WALL.what: The film's own screens tiled at a slight angle in their glass windows, dimmed and softened by the products' strongest glass blur, drifting slowly sideways behind the Block 14 phrases.

G-LISTING.name: The listing card
G-LISTING.what: A plain property-site card (no product's brand): the image P, the address line, four facts and small status chips.

G-CLOCK.name: The desktop clock
G-CLOCK.what: A small clock in the corner of today's desktop that runs from Monday to Wednesday through Block 03.

G-BRIDGE.name: The bridges
G-BRIDGE.what: Dashed lines that try to join two plain document lists and break; a document dragged across by hand.

G-SATELLITE.name: The continent from orbit
G-SATELLITE.what: Australia in NASA's Blue Marble Next Generation colour with its shaded relief multiplied in, graded toward night (deeper oceans, lifted ranges, a low warm sun from the north-west), laid on a plane the camera views in perspective and falls toward; a thin haze of atmosphere at the horizon, a vignette, and the relief sharpening as the camera nears. Public-domain imagery: no street is named on it.

G-PINS.name: The pins
G-PINS.what: Hundreds of white location pins, a stem and a head with a soft shadow on the land and a pinpoint of light, placed where Australians live and landing in waves with a small bounce; one turns gold, rises out of the field and pulses a ring while the rest dim.

G-STAGE.name: The stage in depth
G-STAGE.what: Windows and documents set in a space instead of on a flat page: the site's own perspective (its grid-forward keyframe), a few degrees of turn, soft shadows on a ground that fades into the distance (paper white for today's tools, the brand's night after), depth of field on what is not the subject, and camera moves with motion blur.

G-TICKER.name: The market ticker
G-TICKER.what: A strip of listings and prices scrolling across today's desktop (New listing · Price guide updated · Auction result) in the system face, speeding up as the pressure builds.

G-PHONE.name: The phone
G-PHONE.what: A plain phone face up on the desk, its lock screen lighting with the client's follow-up: no product's brand, the system's own type.

G-PORTAL-SPOTLIGHT.name: One portal at a time
G-PORTAL-SPOTLIGHT.what: Each portal comes forward on its own, almost the frame's width and turned slightly in depth, its dashboard live and its name above it in the eyebrow's mono at display size with a gold rule drawing under it; then it swings into its place in an orbit around the hub as the next comes forward, a line of light running from the hub to it.

G-PAGE-SCROLL.name: The pages, running past
G-PAGE-SCROLL.what: The report's pages travel past the camera one after another in depth, each with the document's own deep shadow, slowing on each long enough to read its headline figure.

G-LIGHT-SWEEP.name: The light sweep
G-LIGHT-SWEEP.what: A band of gold light, the hairline's colour with the traveller's glow, sweeping across the frame on a beat: today's grey tools burn away behind it and the brand's night takes their place.

G-SUNRISE.name: The sunrise
G-SUNRISE.what: A long gold horizon across the navy and the sun clearing it: its disc in the traveller's light, rays fanning up, the sky warming above it.

G-LOGO-JUMP.name: The logo, at the viewer
G-LOGO-JUMP.what: The supplied emblem rushing from small to filling the frame on the products' emphasized ease, with a burst of light and a ring rippling outward, overshooting and settling on their ease-out: the supplied file, never redrawn.

G-CTA.name: The button, alive
G-CTA.what: START YOUR FREE TRIAL on the site's own prismatic button (.btn-chrome-prismatic: its marketing gradient at -45 degrees through gold and cyan, moving on prism-shine), quickened into a pulse, with pulse-glow's gold halo breathing around it; under the pointer it lifts and brightens, and its press is the focus ring's ripple.

G-DEVICES.name: The business in sync
G-DEVICES.what: A laptop, a tablet and a phone in depth, each showing a different portal on the same record; a pulse of light runs between them along the rail line and each screen updates as it arrives.

G-FLOORPLAN.name: The floor plan
G-FLOORPLAN.what: 14 Wattle Grove drawn clean at the frame's own size: walls in solid ink, doors and windows as an architect draws them, every room named and dimensioned, a north point and a scale bar; a sheet that lifts off the page as the document does.

NEW-INBOX.name: A generic inbox
NEW-INBOX.what: Today's tools: a plain mail client with Jordan Ellis's question as the top row, and Reply.

NEW-NOTIFICATIONS.name: Today's notifications
NEW-NOTIFICATIONS.what: Plain toasts from mail, chat, a calendar and a CRM, and the floor plan received for 14 Wattle Grove (PL-03A's item).

NEW-MESSAGE-HUB.name: Command Centre · Message Hub, Jordan Ellis's thread
NEW-MESSAGE-HUB.what: Two states. First, his question from Monday at the top and Alex Morgan's reply typed in the composer, his row in the list reading Draft; then sent, with its delivered tick, and his row moved to Today: Your 14 Wattle Grove report is ready in your portal. Let's go through it together on Thursday.

NEW-CLIENT-REPORTS.what: Two pages. Reports: 14 Wattle Grove, Banksia Rise, Investment Report · Compass, New, with Download Report. My Appointments: Report walkthrough with Alex Morgan, Thu, 22 Oct 2026, 10:00 AM – 10:30 AM, Upcoming.

NEW-DASHBOARDS.what: Each portal's home page with the demo record. Shah Legal (Priya Shah): Welcome back, Open matters, 1 active matter; Ellis: Purchase, 14 Wattle Grove in Contract review, marked Watch after 13 days in the stage. NEW-REPORT-CHARTS.what: The product's report in its own unbranded colours (white pages under the issuer's running head, gold #D9A520 and obsidian #251F18), drawn as figures instead of prose: the cover with A+ beside the address; Key figures (purchase price $1,150,000, weekly rent $850, gross yield 3.8 percent, ten-year median growth); capital growth, the council area's median price across ten years as a line; the ten-year cash flow in bars; How this grade was reached, A+ on a dial and its five dimensions as bars, composite 84; the suburb at a glance in figures and icons; rental comparables on a chart; the risk dashboard in levels. shots.title: Somewhere in Australia, one pin turns gold
shots.camera: A slow orbit across the continent, then one fall from orbit to the suburb, easing in; the card ends in the upper action zone with the gold pin under it.
shots.result: The property's card, readable, above its gold pin on the satellite map.
shots.notes: The pins are where Australians live (the ABS's population by statistical area, thinned to about 600 pins), so the east coast glows and the interior stays dark. The imagery is NASA's Blue Marble Next Generation and its shaded relief, public domain; nothing on it names a real street.
voiceover: a property opportunity has just appeared.

beats.do: The continent from orbit: Australia in satellite colour and relief, tilted away from the camera in depth, a low warm sun from the north-west raking its ranges, the oceans deepening to the horizon under a thin haze of atmosphere. Already falling into it: white location pins, a few, then hundreds, each landing with a small bounce, a soft shadow on the land and a pinpoint of light, dense along the east coast and around the five capitals, sparse across the interior.
The rain of pins thickens into the coastal cities; every pin is the same white.

One pin on the New South Wales coast, north-west of Sydney, turns gold: it rises out of the field, a ring pulses out from it once, and every other pin dims a little. The camera begins to fall toward it.

The camera arrives over Sydney's north-west, the relief sharpening as it nears; the gold pin's head opens and the property pops up from it on a spring: the photograph P, 14 Wattle Grove, Banksia Rise NSW 2155, four facts, a New listing chip.
The card settles, lifted off the map by its own shadow, the gold pin still standing beneath it.

Can we review whether this suits my plans?
voiceover: A client wants to know if it's right for them,
while there's still time to act.

beats.do: The card shrinks into a link preview in a plain messaging window that swings in from the right, in depth: from Jordan Ellis to Alex Morgan, today's tools in daylight greys, its shadow soft on the paper-white desk beneath.
The question types itself in at a reading pace, the window turning gently toward the camera as it does.
The pointer reaches Send and presses it: the window's own pressed state, then Sent, and the message lifts into its thread.
On the attached card a small chip appears: Expressions of interest close Friday.

production.how: Each shot is one HTML composition at 1080 x 1920: the plate builders' own pages (scripts/aurixa-reel-1/portals.cjs, built from the products' code) placed in the graphics kit's window, with a timeline that sets every element's state at time t from the shot's beats in brief.json.

Frame by frame in Chromium (Playwright): set t = frame / 30, let the page lay out, capture, and encode at 30 fps with ffmpeg (H.264, yuv420p, high quality; an overlay with transparency as ProRes 4444). Deterministic: the same brief renders the same film, and a change to one shot re-renders only that shot.

The kit's colours, type, radii, shadows, glass and motion come from one stylesheet written from the four Aurixa repositories' own code (see The design system, from the code), not from values picked by eye.

scripts/aurixa-reel-1/render.cjs draws the whole reel, shot by shot from scenes/, and encodes it as one master with its soundtrack: the method the client approved on 22 October 2026 after the proof of 04.1 to 05.2. The studio's Editor is not in the picture's path.

National Treasures under the whole film and the voiceover held open in its silences (pacing.py), laid out as a studio edit's audio items on the Editor's mixer channels (the voiceover on its own channel, the music and its four pieces on Music & FX, each with its gain, fades and ducking under speech) and mixed by the studio's own media worker code, with two-pass loudness normalisation (soundtrack.py).

Nothing billed by a provider but the logo's moments: one image edit for its clean plate and the video model's takes (logo-takes.json); the rest is building the kit, the pages and the compositions, then rendering.

review_gates: Style frames: one still per block, at its key beat, in the final look. Approve before anything moves.
Animatic: the shots as timed stills on the voiceover, with the captions. Approve the timing before the final renders.
First render: the full reel in the Editor as a draft, then shot by shot changes.

decisions.detail: National Treasures is the client's choice (22 October 2026) and is in the film. Its licence for paid or public use is the client's to confirm before the film runs anywhere but review.

If the client can record the live Command Centre on the demo workspace, those recordings can replace any composition one for one. The code-built pages are the default because they are exact, fictional and ready now.
Blocks 01 to 03 are deliberately unbranded and light, so Block 04's turn to navy and gold reads as Aurixa arriving. The alternative is to open in the brand's navy and keep the problem in muted tones.
